decision: I chose OpenAI chat model 'gpt-3.5-turbo' (via OPENAI_API_KEY) for the eligibility and consent agents.
reason: gpt-3.5-turbo is broadly available, lower-cost for samples, and supported by LangChain; it is adequate for small summarization and rationale tasks in a sample app.

decision: I chose to read the DocumentDB connection string from the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime (no secrets in repo).
alternatives: Read DB credentials from a file
Read DB connection URI from environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI
reason: Security best practice and the run environment already provides DOCUMENTDB_URI; the prompt forbids writing secrets to files.
evidence: Skill_md: 'Its connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI. Read it from the environment at run time.'

decision: I chose not to provision any Azure resources and to use the existing cluster pointed to by DOCUMENTDB_URI.
alternatives: Provision a new Azure DocumentDB cluster (Bicep/Terraform)
Use the existing, reachable cluster described in the run environment
reason: Provisioning is disallowed by run policy and an existing cluster is available for the sample to use; avoid creating paid resources.
evidence: Readiness report and run environment: 'a cluster is already provisioned and reachable' and run policy: 'Azure resource changes allowed: False.'

decision: I chose to create scalar indexes for query prefiltering (criteria.conditions, criteria.min_age, criteria.max_age) via pymongo, and to attempt creating a vector index of kind 'vector-hnsw' with dimensions 1536 via the documentdb MCP server; if the MCP create-index call fails, the sample will fall back to client-side ranking using stored embeddings.
alternatives: Also create a vector index with kind vector-hnsw using dimensions matching embedding model
reason: Scalar indexes speed prefilters; vector index creation requires the exact MCP call format so we'll try it programmatically and gracefully handle failure for verification in this environment.
evidence: Readiness report guidance: 'Create vector indexes using the service's createIndexes runCommand with cosmosSearchOptions ... set dimensions to match chosen embedding model.'

decision: I chose to allow the seed script to run without OPENAI_API_KEY by generating random normalized vectors of dimension 1536 when the key is not present.
alternatives: Require OPENAI_API_KEY for seed to generate embeddings
Allow seed to run without an embedding key by generating random vectors of the chosen dimension
reason: This enables the sample to be seeded and verified in environments where an embedding API key is not available while preserving the ability to produce real embeddings when the key is provided.
evidence: Readiness report: 'Information gap: embedding model and dimensionality ... builder must decide' and run environment may not have OPENAI_API_KEY set.

decision: I attempted to create a service-side vector index via the documentdb MCP server but the create-index call failed; I will record this failure and continue using client-side ranking of stored embeddings as a fallback.
alternatives: Record failure and fall back to client-side ranking
reason: Service-side vector index creation via the MCP helper failed in this environment; sample remains functional using client-side ranking and scalar indexes created by the seed script.
